topIssues.title: supernode: Clear Verifications and Denied Blocks on L1 Reorg
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
L1 consistency is currently handled two ways in the supernode:
- Virtual Nodes handle their L1 chain independently and will discover reorgs and react naturally
- Interop Activity watches the "CurrentL1" of all chains

But this is insufficient.
If the L1 reorgs, there are two groups of data which need to be pruned:
- denylist: previously denied blocks may become valid with new L1
- verification and logs: previously approved blocks may become invalid with new L1

During the consistency check phase, we need to detect L1 reorg and prune this data.

We should also consider who owns this signaling. If every Verification Activity did it on its own, this would be be very noisy. Maybe there should be an L1 watcher for activities...

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Prune Denylist on L1 Reorg and Alert
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
We need to ensure that whenever the Virtual Node responds to an L1 reorg, all downstream components prune data:

Chain Containers must prune their `Denylist` - if not, then a legitimate Unsafe chain could be denied inappropriately

Activities need to be notified via the same `Reset` callback already used. This is because they need to prune their verification results and logs.
Related: Related to: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19287

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Prune Interop Database on L1 Reorg
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
Currently, when the L1 reorgs, there is no attempt from the interop activity to remove old data.

The individual virtual nodes will respond to reorgs, and that in turn will clear out the individual log databases and verification data. However, if L1 inconsistency is not understood by the supernode, it could potentially represent situations where some virtual nodes are on a divergent L1 view.

Note that this is exceedingly unlikely in an application sense because all Virtual Nodes share an L1 connection. However, if an L1 were to reorg as logs were collected, an inconsistent view of that particular timestamp could be constructed. This would cause a "Safe" view of the data which is hiding inconsistency.

To address this, we should slightly expand the CurrentL1 tracking to:
- Confirm CurrentL1 values are all canonical with one-another
- Confirm L1 values did not change during the operation

Some of this consistency checking is already done in the interop activity.


Far-Future Note:
Many of the operational patterns of tracking the CurrentL1 and providing L2 timestamped data are generic to all Verification Activities. Therefore, many of the structs and runtime patterns in it SHOULD be moved upward so that each VA can feature a minimal definition of how to setup and run. Not the purpose of this ticket, but as we think about ensuring L1 consistency, we should consider that actually this could be supplied at a level above activities themselves.

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): in-memory overlay state with async persistence [WIP]
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
# Description

**Summary**

Replaces the direct-to-disk write path in `LiveTrieCollector` with a write-buffer architecture. Blocks are now accumulated in an in-memory buffer and flushed to disk asynchronously by a dedicated persistence service. An overlay provider allows block execution to read from buffered state that hasn't been persisted yet, decoupling execution throughput from disk I/O latency.

** Motivation**

Previously, every call to `execute_and_store_block_updates` or `store_block_updates` opened a read-write transaction, wrote the diff, and committed synchronously. This made block processing throughput directly bottlenecked by disk write speed. 

This PR:
- Decouples block execution from disk writes, so the ExEx can process blocks at EVM speed while I/O happens in the background
- Batches multiple block diffs into a single write transaction, reducing transaction overhead
- Moves pruning into the same write transaction as persistence, eliminating the separate prune task and its race window
- Introduces backpressure so the buffer doesn't grow unbounded if persistence falls behind

Architecture
```
ExEx loop ──► LiveTrieCollector (in-memory buffer)
                  │
                  │ advance_persistence() when buffer ≥ threshold
                  ▼
              std::thread::spawn ──► LiveTriePersistenceHandle
                                         │
                                         │ crossbeam channel
                                         ▼
                                    LiveTriePersistenceService (background thread)
                                         │
                                         ├─ batch write (store_trie_updates_batch)
                                         ├─ prune (prune_with_provider)
                                         └─ commit
```

**Tests**

Pending

**Additional context**

NA

**Metadata**

Blocked on https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19928

# Notes 

We should refactor(this or another PR) LiveTrieCollector into an engine:
- LiveTrieCollectorEngine — a private struct that owns all mutable state and runs a single-threaded message loop on a dedicated thread. Processes a CollectorAction enum (ExecuteAndStore, StoreBlockUpdates, UnwindAndStore, UnwindHistory, WaitForPersistence, GetTipBlockNumber) sequentially, structurally enforcing the serial-call invariant.
- LiveTrieCollectorHandle — a thin, clonable Sender<CollectorAction> wrapper that is the only public type. Every method sends a message + blocks on a one-shot reply channel, preserving the existing synchronous API.

This eliminates:
- `PersistenceStatus` (Mutex + Condvar) — persistence tracking becomes engine-local (persist_in_flight: bool + persist_reply_rx: Option<Receiver>)
- parking_lot dependency from this module
- Throwaway `std::thread::spawn` per flush — the engine sends directly to the persistence service

topPRs.title: interop: add OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator for post-migration validation
topPRs.author: stevennevins
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Add `OPContractsManagerMigrationValidator`, a new contract to validate L1 contract configuration after an interop migration (`opcm.migrate()`). This verifies that shared infrastructure (DGF, ASR, ETHLockbox, DelayedWETH) and per-chain cross-references are correctly set up.

Separated from `OPContractsManagerStandardValidator` due to EIP-170 contract size limits.

Closes #16033

## Details

Stacked on #19840.

### New entry points

- `validateMigration(MigrationValidationInput, bool)` — validates shared infra once + each chain
- `validateMigrationWithOverrides(...)` — same with `ValidationOverrides` support

### Current state

This PR adds the contract scaffold with stub implementations. Validation logic will be added incrementally.

topPRs.title: refactor(kona): remove native rollup-boost support
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Remove `rollup-boost` and `rollup-boost-types` crate dependencies from the kona workspace
- Route all Engine API v3/v4 calls (`new_payload`, `fork_choice_updated`, `get_payload`) directly to the L2 execution engine instead of through a rollup-boost middleware proxy
- Remove rollup-boost CLI flags (`--rollup-boost-execution-mode`, `--flashblocks`, builder client args, etc.), RPC endpoints (`setExecutionMode`, `getExecutionMode`, `kona-rollup-boost.healthz`), and all supporting types/traits

Operators who need rollup-boost functionality (block builders, flashblocks, execution mode management) can run rollup-boost as a standalone sidecar and point kona-node's `--l2` engine URL at it.

**33 files changed, -1458 lines net**

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --workspace` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes with no warnings
- [x] `rg "rollup.boost" rust/kona/` returns zero matches in source files
- [ ] CI passes

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-tests: refactor flashblocks tests
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
## Summary

  - Introduce `sources.FlashblockClient` in `op-service/sources/flashblock_client.go` — a reusable wrapper around a WebSocket connection that reads raw messages, unmarshals them into typed `*Flashblock`
   values, and delivers them on a channel. This moves the `Flashblock` type and its custom `UnmarshalJSON` (which lowercases `new_account_balances` keys) out of the test package and into `op-service`
  where it can be shared.
  - Refactor `TestFlashblocksStream` to use `FlashblockClient` and simplify the assertions: spin up two goroutines (one per stream source), consume typed flashblocks, and verify that block numbers and
  indices always increase. Removes the old duration-based collection, manual JSON unmarshalling, tolerance counting, and `evaluateFlashblocksStream` helper.
  - Refactor `TestFlashblocksTransfer` to use `FlashblockClient` and a reactive pattern: stream flashblocks until one contains Bob's updated balance, then wait for the transaction to confirm and assert
  correctness. Removes the old 20-second timed collection, `timedMessage` struct, and post-hoc scanning loop.
  - Clean up `utils.go`: remove the now-relocated `Flashblock` type, its `UnmarshalJSON`, `FlashblocksStreamMode` constants, and unexport `DriveViaTestSequencer` → `driveViaTestSequencer`. Add a shared
  `startClient` helper for test lifecycle management.

topPRs.title: fix(kona-node): handle missing L1 origin block in sequencer instead of panicking
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
The origin selector could panic with `unreachable!()` when
`get_block_by_hash` returned `Ok(None)` — e.g. during an L1 reorg or
sync lag. Replace the panic with an `OriginNotFound` error and trigger
an engine reset in the sequencer actor so the node recovers gracefully.

A real-world example of this bug is in [this] ci run.

[this]: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121941/workflows/391e49ef-49fb-4a52-a18b-c73e3bb0ee9d/jobs/4753970/tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
